notes: The centre and the first vertex. There are two given points, so the construction is general: any other choice of them gives a similar figure.

steps.text: P0' = meet x u except P0
A = meet y u left O P0
notes: The axes, and $A = (0, 1)$, the common end of all Carlyle diameters.
$c_1$ is the Carlyle circle of $u^2 + u/2 - 1 = 0$, whose roots are $eta/2$: its diameter runs from $(0, 1)$ to $(-1/2, -1)$, so its centre is $K$. Hence $V = (eta_1/2, 0)$ and $W = (eta_0/2, 0)$.
For $p = -1$ the Carlyle centre $(s/2, 0)$ lies on the axis. So $c_2$ is the Carlyle circle of $x^2 - eta_0 x - 1 = 0$, and $M_1 = (mu_1, 0)$, $M_0 = (mu_0, 0)$.
Likewise $c_3$ is the Carlyle circle of $x^2 - eta_1 x - 1 = 0$: $N_1 = (nu_1, 0)$ and $N_0 = (nu_0, 0)$.

steps.text: N0y = meet y cn left O P0

notes: $B = (mu_0, nu_0)$, the far end of the last Carlyle diameter.
$c_4$ is the Carlyle circle of $x^2 - mu_0 x + nu_0 = 0$. So $X_4 = (c_4, 0)$ and $X_1 = (c_1, 0) = (2 cos(2 pi / 17), 0)$.

steps.text: P1 = meet g u left O P0
notes: $G = (cos(2 pi / 17), 0)$, so $P_1 = (cos(2 pi / 17), sin(2 pi / 17))$ is the second vertex.
Each further vertex comes from the circle centred at the last vertex through the one before.
Stepping the chord $P_0 P_1$ around the circle closes up after 17 steps.

notes: All 17 sides are equal. All vertices lie on the circle $u$ by construction.

Every other vertex lies to the left of the side $P_0 P_1$. So the step angle is $2 pi / 17$, not $2 pi k / 17$ with $k >= 2$ (a star polygon would have vertices on both sides of $P_0 P_1$): the polygon is the convex regular 17-gon.
